CLEAN-UP JUST BEGUN.

Spooners on the Sands to F

ollow the Grist of “Social

Vagrants”—Parson Mason Starts Something, Too.
Police Judge Hart Declares for Full Publicity—Com-
mittee that Doesn’t Come to “The Times.”

ONG BEACH, Nov. 21—A minor-:
ity of ¢itizens, who, believing in
profit in city lots and a whited
sepulcher, sought to “hush up” the
news of official record about the
“social vagrants,” were aghast today
when they learned that the campaign
for cleaning this city has just, begun.
Announcement came from an official
source that the Mayor and Police
Commission purpose to raid the beach
front next, and some citizens who
are pretty well known may become
prey to the police dragnet.
While Mayor Whealton and Police
Commissioners W. H- Wallace and
W. M. VandeWater are trying to
“open the canker and ‘let the rotten-
ness out,” as the Mayor,says, there
are others deep in city property who
seek to discredit the municipal house-

cleaning. ’ :
Rev. 0. H. L. Mason—it is he who
resigned .trom nis pulpit in the
First Presbyterian Church after

charges were filed against him, ac-
cusing him of becoming unduly friend-
ly with a young girl in his congrega-
tlon—has called a mass.meeting at
the .forum for Monday night, The
Rey. Mr. Mason, who now conducts 4
church of his own in the eastern part
of the city, will address this meeting,
and has chosen for his subject, “The
Barbarous, Bestial and Brutal’ Press,
or, Some Local Tragedies.” The Rev.
Mr. ‘Mason will not, it is understood,
refer in his “address, to his .conduct
With the innocent girl. .
_ | WOULD PLANT CACTUS, *
It §s stated in officlaldom that the
beautiful stretch of sand'which is the
pride of Long Beach is defiled nightly
by scores of men and: women whose
spooning ig offensive in the eyes of
the police and is against the law. .A
“purity squad” will be put on by the
officials to make arrests under or-
dinance No, 681, which makes it a
misdemeanor to spoon on the sand,
“If necessary,” said a member of
the Police Commission today, “we will
plant cactus on every foot of the sand
within the city of Long Beach, and
We Will see to it thnt it is noc of tne
spineless variety. .We have started to
clean up the city, and now that we
have had the publicity, let us have
the benefit. There is no use dodging
the fact that there 1s rottenness in the
city. Let us rid ourselves of the con-
dition.
“No wonder the people of Los An-
geles and other cities around us con-
sider us hypocrites. Before the last:
election there were many of the parsi-
monious who were the loudest in their.
denunciation of ‘The Demon Rum,’
and we knew all the time that they
served beer on their tables at meals.”
‘W. H. Warren and B. C, Brown, the
special ‘officers who secured the evi-
dence for the arrest of thirty-one
men on the charge of vagrancy, which
charge covers unprintable sins, dre
still members of the police force, and
wiil remain, for the time being. . They
will probably continue the work for
which they were engaged and bring
more “social vagrants” to the bar of
Justice,
LOWE CASE UP TUESDAY. *

The caso of Herbert N. Lowe, the

last of the famous thirty-one “social
vagrants,” will be reopened before
Justice Underwood Tuesday morning,
when an argument by Attorney Swaf-
field to dismiss hig client, on the
ground that he had been once in
jeopardy on the charge, will be heard.
It is probable that the case of Lowe
will-end on that day. Nothing will,
then remain of the celebrated cases
except the $5275 in. fines ‘collected
from the thirty-one, and seven “un-
fortunates” now serving _ six-months’
sentence in the County Jall.
“John A. Lamb was guilty,
Police Judge J. J, Hart, toda:
was as guilty of the charge of vagran-
cy as any of’ the group, although we
all deplore his death. we
“Mr, Lamb, confessed his guilt at
the time he appeared before me. I
have known for some time of the
gullt of this defendant, and it has been
of knowledge. to other men,
“I am‘in favor-of publishing the
names and acts of these degenerates.
Let the cases be sent. broadcast, print-
ed in huge letters, and show up the
wickedness. Publicity for these kind,
of cases Js the greatest aid to the sup-
pression;of the vice.” - : : ‘
At theimeeting of the Chamber of
Commerce’ - yesterday, Justice S. H.
Underwood, who was trying the case
against Lowe, led in the denuncla-
tion of the publication of the case of
Lowe, and ‘those who had gone be-
fore, to leave from $100 to $500 each
in the. city: treasury. Justice,
Underwood took occasion, in the
course ‘of his remarks, to denounce
The ‘Times and its publication of the
official facts about the degenerates in
Long Beach. He favored a resolution
arraigning The Times, and although
most of the directors present appeared
to want The Times’ denounced for
printing the news of the day without
fear or favor, he got only a weak
second, and no resolution,
Then someone arose to move that
the directors go as a committee of
the whole to Gen. Otls, and demand
that he publish no more articles re-:
garding crime -in Long Beach. This
was at first favored, but the discus-
sion resolved itself into a resolution
appointing Postmaster W. J. Des--
mond, P. B, Hatch and I. R. Hall a
committee to go to The Times and
protest, But two,members of this
committee have decided not to go, and
the matter has been dropped, at least
for the present. ,
, Attorney R. G, Swaffield stated to-
day that-he had under consideration
a motion for a change of venue or
like legal ‘move, because of expres-
sions ‘made by Justice Underwood at
the Chamber. of Commerce meeting.
The attorney understands that the
justice violated the Clvil Code in dis-
cussing the case in which’he was pre-
siding, -Justice: Underwood incignant-~
jy ‘denied that he had discussed the
Lowe’ case. He admitted having ar-
raigned ‘The Times for printing the
“social vagrant cases.” but he stated |
that-he did not specialize on the Lowe
case in hig remarks.
{The Times Is, as: usual, fighting
in the open. It is ready for the “vis-
itation” of the committee either of
